proof_summary: Composite moduli are excluded by splitting off powers of two: for a proper odd prime divisor \(p\mid n\), multiplicative-order counts and Legendre’s formula give the strict \(p\)-adic valuation needed to show \(p\mid a(n-1)\), contradicting divisibility of the sum, while for \(n=2^k\) a binary-digit valuation calculation gives \(v_2(a(n-1))=k-1\). For prime \(n\), the defining product identity, Wilson’s theorem, and the assumed congruence yield \(\prod_{j=1}^{n-2}(2^j-1)\equiv1\pmod n\); hence the order of \(2\) cannot be less than \(n-1\), since its corresponding factor would vanish, so it equals \(n-1\).
